## What is the Gladly MCP Server?

 A Gladly MCP server lets AI agents read and write Gladly data through the [Model Context Protocol](/platform/mcp/) — Anthropic's open standard for connecting LLMs to external tools. StackOne's Gladly MCP server ships with 65 pre-built actions, fully extensible via the [Connector Builder](/platform/ai-integration-builder/) — plus managed authentication, prompt injection defense, observability, and agent execution runtime. Connect it from MCP clients like [Claude Desktop](/platform/mcp/ai-agent/claude-desktop/), [Claude Code](/platform/mcp/ai-agent/claude-code/), [Cursor](/platform/mcp/ai-agent/cursor/), [Goose](/platform/mcp/ai-agent/goose/), and VS Code, or from agent frameworks like OpenAI Agents SDK, LangChain, and Vercel AI SDK.

## All Gladly MCP Tools

 Every action from Gladly's API, ready for your agent. Create, read, update, and delete — scoped to exactly what you need.

## Gladly MCP Server FAQ

 Does StackOne have a Gladly MCP server?
Yes. StackOne offers a hosted Gladly MCP server with 65 pre-built actions, and every action is tested and QA'd by StackOne. Connect it to [Claude](/platform/mcp/ai-agent/claude-desktop/), [Cursor](/platform/mcp/ai-agent/cursor/), and any other [MCP client](/platform/mcp/), or to any agent framework through the [AI Action SDK](https://docs.stackone.com/agents/typescript/introduction). It ships with managed [agent authentication](/platform/agent-auth/), [prompt injection defense](/platform/prompt-injection-guard/), and [tool discovery](/platform/tools-discovery/) with [server-side execution](/platform/agent-execution-engine/) that preserve your agent's context window and keep reasoning performance.

 Gladly MCP server vs direct API integration — what's the difference?
A Gladly MCP server and [direct API integration](/connectors/gladly/) serve different use cases. Direct API integration is for software-to-software — backend code calling Gladly. A Gladly MCP server is for AI agents — [MCP clients](/platform/mcp/) like Claude and Cursor, plus framework agents built with OpenAI, LangChain, or Vercel AI — discovering and calling Gladly at runtime. StackOne provides both.

 How does Gladly authentication work for AI agents?
Gladly [authentication for AI agents](/platform/agent-auth/) works through a StackOne Connect Session. Create one via the dashboard or the SDK — you get an auth link and ready-to-paste config for Claude Desktop, Cursor, and other MCP clients. Your user authenticates their own Gladly account; StackOne handles token exchange, storage, and refresh. Credentials never reach the LLM, and each user is isolated via `origin_owner_id`.

 Are Gladly MCP tools vulnerable to prompt injection?
Yes — Gladly MCP tools can be vulnerable to [indirect prompt injection](/blog/indirect-prompt-injection-mcp-tools-defense/). Any tool that reads user-written content — documents, messages, tickets, records, or free-text fields — is a potential vector. StackOne [Defender](/platform/prompt-injection-guard/) scans every tool response before it enters the agent's context — regex patterns in ~1ms, then a MiniLM classifier in ~4ms. 88.7% accuracy, CPU-only.

 What is the context bloat of a Gladly agent and how do I avoid it?
[Context bloat](/blog/mcp-token-optimization/) happens when Gladly tool schemas and API responses eat your Gladly agent's memory, preventing it from reasoning effectively. A single Gladly query can return a massive JSON response, and connecting multiple tools compounds the problem. [Tools Discovery](/platform/tools-discovery/) and Code Mode reduce context bloat — loading only relevant tools per query and keeping raw responses out of the agent's context.

 Can I limit which actions my Gladly agent can access?
Yes — you can limit which actions your Gladly agent can access directly from the StackOne dashboard. Toggle actions on or off, or restrict them to specific accounts, with no code changes to your agent. [Session tokens](/platform/agent-auth/) can be scoped to exact actions so if one leaks, exposure stays contained.

 Can I create custom agent actions for my Gladly MCP server?
Yes — you can create custom agent actions for your Gladly MCP server using [Connector Builder](/platform/ai-integration-builder/). It's an integration agent your coding assistant (Claude Code, Cursor, or Copilot) can invoke to research Gladly's API, generate production-ready connector YAML, test against the live API, and validate before you ship.

 When should I NOT use a Gladly MCP server?
Skip a Gladly MCP server if your integration is purely software-to-software — [direct Gladly API integration](/connectors/gladly/) is simpler when no AI agent is involved. For deterministic, compliance-critical operations (financial transactions, regulatory reporting), direct API gives you predictable behavior without agent-driven decision-making. MCP shines when AI agents need to dynamically discover and call Gladly actions at runtime.

 What AI frameworks and AI clients does the StackOne Gladly MCP server support?
The StackOne Gladly [MCP server](/platform/mcp/) supports both. **MCP clients** (paste-and-go apps): [Claude Desktop](/platform/mcp/ai-agent/claude-desktop/), [Claude Code](/platform/mcp/ai-agent/claude-code/), [Cursor](/platform/mcp/ai-agent/cursor/), VS Code, [Goose](/platform/mcp/ai-agent/goose/). **Agent frameworks** (code SDKs you build with): OpenAI Agents SDK, Anthropic, Vercel AI, Google ADK, CrewAI, Pydantic AI, LangChain, LangGraph, Azure AI Foundry.
